questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole square cut into 100 equal small squares. Emma colours 7 of the small squares green and leaves the other 93 white. Which choice shows the green part as a fraction and as a decimal?
questions.explain: 7 shaded squares out of 100 equal squares is 7 hundredths, so the fraction is 7/100 and the 7 sits in the hundredths place: 0.07. The trap is copying the 7 straight after the point to get 0.7, but 0.7 is 7 tenths, which would be 70 shaded squares.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole square cut into 100 equal small squares. Liam shades 50 of the small squares red. Which choice shows the red part as a fraction and as a decimal?
questions.explain: 50 shaded squares out of 100 equal squares is 50 hundredths: 50/100 = 0.50, which is half the grid. Watch out for sliding the digits over — 0.05 would mean only 5 shaded squares.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole square cut into 100 equal small squares. Priya shades 80 of the small squares blue. Which choice shows the blue part as a fraction and as a decimal?
questions.explain: 80 shaded out of 100 equal squares is 80/100, and 80 hundredths is written 0.80. The pair that says 8/100 and 0.8 just copies the digit 8 after the point; 8/100 would be only 8 shaded squares.

questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole square cut into 100 equal small squares. Rosa colours 4 of the small squares purple, so the purple part is 4/100 of the whole grid. Which decimal is the same amount?
questions.explain: 4/100 means 4 hundredths, so the 4 goes in the hundredths place, two spots after the point: 0.04. Writing 0.4 copies the digit into the tenths place, and that would mean 40 of the 100 squares were coloured.

questions.question: Jayden buys a sticker at the school store for $0.45. One whole dollar is 100 cents. Which fraction of a dollar did Jayden spend?
questions.explain: Two digits after the decimal point means hundredths, so $0.45 is 45 hundredths of a dollar: 45/100. The trap is copying 45 over a 10 — the fraction 45/10 would be more than four whole dollars.

questions.question: Ana ran 7/10 of a kilometre at track practice. Her coach records every distance as a decimal to hundredths. Which decimal should the coach write?
questions.explain: 7/10 is 7 tenths, which is 0.7, and 7 tenths is the same as 70 hundredths, so the coach writes 0.70. Writing 7.10 just copies the 7 and the 10 out of the fraction instead of thinking about place value.

questions.question: Which pair below shows the very same amount written first as a fraction and then as a decimal?
questions.explain: 23/100 is 23 hundredths, and hundredths need two digits after the point, so it is 0.23. Pairs like 5/100 and 0.5 only copy the digits — 0.5 is 50 hundredths, ten times bigger than 5/100.

questions.question: A recipe at Emma's summer camp near Kamloops uses 0.60 L of milk. Which fraction of a litre is exactly the same amount?
questions.explain: 0.60 has two digits after the point, so it is 60 hundredths: 60/100 of a litre. Reading it as 60/10 copies the digits and would mean 6 whole litres of milk.

questions.question: Leo and Maya are both writing 4/100 as a decimal. Leo writes 0.4 and says you just put the top number after the point. Maya writes 0.04. Who is correct?
options: Leo, because 0.4 and 0.04 are the same amount
Neither, because 4/100 as a decimal is 4.00
Maya, because 4/100 is 4 hundredths, so the 4 must sit in the hundredths place
Leo, because the digits from the fraction go straight after the decimal point
questions.explain: 4/100 is 4 hundredths, so the 4 goes two places after the point: 0.04. Leo's shortcut of copying digits gives 0.4, which is 4 tenths, or 40 hundredths — ten times too big.

questions.question: Sofia's community garden plot is one whole rectangle divided into 100 equal squares. She plants carrots in 3 full rows of 10 squares each, and lettuce in 8 more single squares. Which choice shows the planted part as a fraction and as a decimal?
questions.explain: 3 rows of 10 squares is 30 squares, plus 8 more makes 38 out of 100 squares: 38/100 = 0.38. Two common slips are adding 3 + 8 instead of 30 + 8, and sliding the digits so the 3 and 8 no longer sit in the tenths and hundredths places.

questions.question: A juice box in the school cafeteria costs $0.75. Nina writes this as the fraction 75/10 of a dollar. Which choice gives the correct fraction and explains Nina's mistake?
options: 75/1000 of a dollar; she should have used thousandths, since money always needs three places
75/10 of a dollar; she is right, because 75 is what comes after the point and dimes are tenths
75/100 of a dollar; she copied the digits but two places after the point mean hundredths
7/10 of a dollar; she should have used only the first digit after the point and dropped the 5
questions.explain: $0.75 is 75 cents out of the 100 cents in a dollar, so the fraction is 75/100. The number of places after the point tells you the denominator — 75/10 would be seven and a half dollars.

questions.question: On the Stanley Park seawall, Owen says he walked 5/10 of a kilometre and Ivy says she walked 0.50 of a kilometre. Who walked farther?
options: Ivy, because 0.50 has two digits after the point, so it counts more hundredths
Owen, because tenths are always bigger pieces than hundredths
Owen, because 5/10 written as a decimal is 5.10
They walked the same distance, because 5/10 is 0.5, and 0.5 is the same as 0.50
questions.explain: 5/10 is 5 tenths, which is 0.5, and 5 tenths is the same as 50 hundredths, so 0.50 is an equal distance. Extra digits after the point do not make a decimal bigger, and copying the 5 and 10 into 5.10 changes the number completely.
